en: The Sun is so large that about 1.3 million Earths could fit inside it.
The Moon is approximately 384,400 kilometers away from Earth on average.
Diamond is the hardest natural mineral on Earth, scoring a perfect ten on the Mohs scale.
About 97 percent of all water on Earth is salty ocean water, leaving only three percent as freshwater.
Typhoon Haiyan in 2013 produced some of the highest recorded wind speeds, reaching 315 kilometers per hour.
Proxima Centauri is the closest star to our solar system, located about 4.24 light-years away.
Topsoil, the uppermost soil layer, usually takes about 500 years to naturally form just one inch.
Mount Taal is one of the smallest but most active volcanoes in the Philippines, standing only 311 meters tall.
Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system, measuring about 11 times wider than Earth.
Magma inside the Earth can reach extremely high temperatures of up to 1,300 degrees Celsius.
An average cumulus cloud can weigh about 500,000 kilograms, which is equal to 100 elephants.
The Sun is exactly 400 times larger than the Moon, but also 400 times farther away.
